C01.signature: Service binds selected video and caption snapshots to a persistent, recognizable request/result identity; workers use those inputs and editors select that identity despite completion reversals. Several members additionally compare intended, requested, consumed and downloaded pairs or reject mismatches. Predict matching hashes and fewer unintended selections, not necessarily shorter renders. Requires immutable storage, meaningful labels and affordable worker/interface changes; delivered wording remains accessible.
C01.reason: The agreed members all enact or directly test fixed-pair identification; excerpts, tuples and receipts predict compatible hash/selection outcomes. Include H1-F06 for the explicit intent/request/worker/download diagnostic in P001 Z1 and related probes, alongside binding and history identity. This auxiliary overlap does not merge the diagnostic-only C04 family or establish another mechanism.

C02.signature: Analyst partitions final-edit-to-correct-preview time at independently verified intended-output availability, separating selection and viewing afterward. Late readiness versus late identification directs scheduling versus identification work; pending-job replay tests avoidable queue work. Requires attributable events and bounded editor observation; missing historical attention and festival demand remain unknown.
C02.reason: Preserve the agreed family and archive matches: all members test the same availability boundary. P001 Z2 adds replay of omitted pending work, compatible with that discriminator. The minute-15 threshold and single-correction comparisons refine its application.

C03.signature: Private browser plays a selected immutable video/caption pair with timed overlays before the same pair receives embedded rendering. Earlier faithful inspection can avoid intermediate full renders if waiting matters; compare cue wording, timing and layout against the embedder. Requires usable private playback, adequate fidelity and an affordable prototype; preserve embedded delivery and prior wording.
C03.reason: All four members compare selected-pair overlays with embedded playback; frozen handoff and cue fidelity are pairwise compatible. Preserve agreed equivalence to overlay and input-binding operations. Extra comparison arms in P002 A2 do not establish a distinct causal interaction.

C04.signature: Analyst traces independently confirmed intent through requested pair, worker inputs, output and download during overlapping-job replay. First divergence before rendering supports capture/binding failure; correct production followed by unintended download supports selection failure. Both or neither may occur. Requires comparable hashes and independent intent; absent historical fields remain unresolved.
C04.reason: Preserve the agreed diagnostic family. All three members distinguish pre-render identity divergence from later unintended selection using independently captured intention. They pose the archived input-selection question, including when written as a hypothesis.

C05.signature: Browser seeks changed caption cues with surrounding motion and overlays selected captions before an explicit full embedded render. Local inspection may reduce review and render demand; context expansion or disagreement in planted-error detection and final playback tests inadequate context/fidelity. Requires private seeking, meaningful surrounding motion, faithful cues and affordable implementation. Full embedded delivery and prior wording remain available.
C05.reason: All three members direct immediate inspection to changed cues plus surrounding motion. Include H1-F03 because P005 A2 explicitly replaces every-save rendering with an explicit request, also compatible with P008/P009. H1-F04 supplies the overlay component; local-context sufficiency preserves agreed local novelty. Unchanged delay alone cannot identify selection/viewing as the cause, as P005 suggests.

C06.signature: Service uses the same immutable manifest/generation to replace unstarted requests and allow only still-intended completions to acquire the current-preview pointer, retaining older outputs and a separate delivered record. During bursts and completion inversions, predict fewer obsolete dispatches than binding alone and fewer wrong-current selections than coalescing alone. Requires replaceable pending work, affordable conditional publication and understandable identities.
C06.reason: Preserve the agreed family and local novelty. Each member explicitly couples pending-work eligibility and current-publication eligibility through the same identity; this is present directly in all three texts, not inferred transitively. Archived binding, identification and demand reduction are constituents; benefit and superadditivity remain untested.

C07.signature: Editor saves drafts immediately but explicitly requests full preview rendering; one member captures the chosen source pair and displays saved-draft/request differences. Consolidating saves reduces renders; latency improves only when avoided work causes queue delay, while forgotten requests or extra friction can worsen it. Requires acceptable editor behavior and affordable trigger changes; retain delivered previews and embedded output.
C07.reason: Both members implement the archived explicit-request trigger and predict savings versus request friction. Include partial H1-F01/H1-F02 overlap for P007 A2 capturing the chosen pair and showing draft/request differences; P010 A2 lacks those optional details but has the same trigger and counterprediction. These overlaps do not create another family.

C08.signature: Analyst crosses interruption with presence of a persistent selected-cut/caption-excerpt receipt while holding labels, waits and completion order fixed. Selective reduction of interruption-related selection errors/time supports remembered-intent continuity. Requires bounded counterbalanced fabricated tasks and independently stipulated targets; two editors provide exploratory evidence only.
C08.reason: Preserve the agreed singleton and local novelty: interruption-by-receipt interaction with waits/labels/order held fixed differs from ordinary source identification. Archive matches describe receipt and tracing components, not the full interaction. No interruption effect has been measured.
